newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates up as supply exceeds demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates up as supply exceeds demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates gained on Saturday and are likely to remain firm because arrival of fresh supplies from the main growing Punjab province have not picked up, dealers said.

"There has been a good crop this year, but it will take some time before cotton supplies from the Punjab province increase," dealer Kishan Chand said. "There has been buying from mill owners and we see the prices to remain firm this week."
In kerb market, dealers said the NIAB-78 variety from the 1996/97 crop was traded in a range of 2,100 ($56.66) and 2,125 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
